scenes.headline: Nobody knows where the bottom is until after
scenes.voiceover: Your cousin says Bitcoin has hit bottom and it's time to buy the dip. The honest answer is that nobody knows where the bottom is until after it has passed. Not analysts, not us. On the nineteenth of November twenty twenty-six, Bitcoin was about sixty-three thousand seven hundred dollars, roughly half its October twenty twenty-five high. So we won't guess. We'll look at ten signals analysts watch: what each one measures, when it was recorded, and where it can be wrong.

scenes.eyebrow: Bitcoin price, US$ · Bloomberg; CoinGecko; Fortune · as of 19 Nov 2026
scenes.headline: From the peak to now
scenes.voiceover: Quick recap. About one hundred and twenty-six thousand dollars at the peak. About sixty thousand in February. A low of fifty-eight thousand five hundred and seventy on the first of July. And around sixty-three thousand seven hundred this week. Now, round one.

scenes.headline: Past lows came about 60 weeks after the peak
scenes.voiceover: Round one: the clock. Blockworks Research found that past bear markets bottomed around sixty weeks after the all-time high. That would put this low at about the end of November twenty twenty-six. The weakness: it's based on only about three past cycles. And if prices keep falling into December, this signal simply runs out.
scenes.name: Round 1

scenes.headline: Past bear markets fell further
scenes.voiceover: Now the ruler. Past Bitcoin bear markets fell between seventy-seven and eighty-five percent from their peaks. This one is about fifty to fifty-three and a half percent so far. The weakness: there's no rule that says this cycle must copy the old ones.
scenes.name: Round 1

scenes.eyebrow: Bitcoin's fall from peak (%) · Bitget; NerdWallet; CoinGecko
scenes.headline: Past bear markets vs this one (so far)
scenes.voiceover: Here's how that looks side by side.

scenes.headline: The July low landed in one analyst's range
scenes.voiceover: Round two: what people paid. The realized price is roughly the average price everyone paid for their Bitcoin. Based on it, CryptoQuant's Julio Moreno said in late twenty twenty-five that the bottom could be between fifty-six and sixty thousand dollars. The July low of fifty-eight thousand five hundred and seventy landed inside that range. But be careful: this is one forecast that happened to land, not proof.
scenes.name: Round 2

scenes.headline: Only 4 of 13 bottom signs had appeared
scenes.receipt: Galaxy Research, published 12 Jun 2026 (data as of 9 Jun 2026)
scenes.voiceover: On the other side, Galaxy Research tracked thirteen signs that have appeared at past bottoms. As of the ninth of June, only four had appeared. The strongest ones, like the price falling below what holders paid, and a big wave of panic selling, had not. This is from June, so it's old, but those missing signs matter.

stat.label: bottom signs present · Galaxy, as of 9 Jun 2026

scenes.name: Round 2

scenes.headline: The fear gauge hit a record low of 5
scenes.receipt: Crypto Fear & Greed Index via CoinGabbar (6 Feb 2026; 4 Nov 2026)

stat.label: Fear & Greed, 6 Feb 2026 · record low since 2018

scenes.voiceover: Round three: the mood. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index scores market mood from zero to one hundred. On the sixth of February it hit five, its lowest reading since tracking began in twenty eighteen. Extreme fear has often come near past lows. It's also one of Galaxy's four signs. But note: by early November it was back at thirty-four. That's ordinary fear, not panic.
scenes.name: Round 3

scenes.headline: Big bets on, or insurance against, $60k
scenes.voiceover: Meanwhile, on the options exchange Deribit, the most popular contract is one that pays out if Bitcoin falls below sixty thousand dollars. Some traders are betting on a drop. Others are simply buying insurance. Either way, many expect more risk ahead.
scenes.name: Round 3

scenes.headline: Miners stopped switching machines off
scenes.receipt: Galaxy Research (Hash Ribbons, early Jun 2026); NewsBTC (difficulty cut, 14 Nov 2026)
scenes.voiceover: Round four: the miners. A signal called Hash Ribbons fired in early June. In plain words: after a stretch where miners were switching machines off, they started switching them back on. That has come before past lows. But on the fourteenth of November, the network's mining difficulty was cut, which can mean some miners are under pressure again. So this one cuts both ways.
scenes.name: Round 4

scenes.headline: US Bitcoin funds lost $1.07bn in a week
scenes.voiceover: And the big money? US exchange-traded funds that hold Bitcoin saw about one point zero seven billion dollars pulled out in the week to the thirteenth of November, with seven trading days of outflows in a row. Big investors were leaving, not arriving.
scenes.name: Round 4

scenes.eyebrow: Round 5 · Same data house, two readings
scenes.headline: CryptoQuant: a "value zone"
scenes.voiceover: Round five shows how messy this is. On the eighteenth of November, the analytics firm CryptoQuant said Bitcoin had reached what it calls a value zone.
scenes.name: Round 5

scenes.headline: …but demand is shrinking fastest since July
scenes.voiceover: But in the very same update, CryptoQuant said Bitcoin is back in a bearish phase, with demand growth shrinking at its fastest pace since July. Same firm, same day, two readings. That's what analysis really looks like.
scenes.name: Round 5

scenes.eyebrow: What to watch, not who to believe
scenes.headline: The signs every true bottom has shown
scenes.body: Price below what holders paid · holders in loss overall · sustained loss-selling · a panic flush
scenes.voiceover: So, has Bitcoin hit bottom? We don't know, and neither does anyone else. Instead of watching for someone's call, watch for what Galaxy says every true bottom has shown, and which hadn't happened as of June: the price falling below what holders paid, holders in loss overall, sustained loss-selling, and a panic flush. Galaxy's own scenarios differ widely. Even they don't know.

scenes.headline: Guaranteed returns? Coin "recovery"? Walk away.
scenes.voiceover: And one warning. Crashes bring scammers. Anyone promising guaranteed crypto returns, or offering to recover coins you've lost, is a red flag.
